messages.subject: Rattle 2.5.23 released - mainly bug fixes
messages.body_plain:
A new version of Rattle has been released with the following
changelog. This is mostly bug fixes.

 * Catch "arules" error in converting data to transactions when
baskets
   contain repeated items.

 * When data tab is executed, and so crs$rpart is reset to NULL,
always
   remove the Draw/Rules button from the Tree option of the Predictive
   tab.

 * Add code to fix translations that are not being loaded when using
   RGtk2 on MS/Windows. All is okay on GNU/Linux, but RGtk2 seems not
to
   get the right locale for loaded Glade file. The fix is to traverse
the
   GUI and change all labels, on starting up Rattle. RGtk2 authors
tried
   to fix but it remains an issue.

 * Ensure rpart is reset on resetting rattle.

 * Rework handling of tab pages because a Japanese translation on
   MS/Windows is having issues with the following call (nd=notebook)
   nb$getTabLabelText(nb$getNthPage(nb$getCurrentPage())) returning
what
   looks like Shift-JIS encoding of the string rather than UTF-8, and
   hence not string matching the expected tab label.

 * Fix spelling errors on help menu and ensure help for all topics is
   covered.

 * For nnet, use MaxNWts=10000 (default is 1000) to allow larger nets
by
   default, and capture the error message when this is exceeded and
   better explain what to do.

 * Ensure we dont export an empty dataset when choosing export on the
   data tab.

 * Capture arules error message when there are repeated items in one
   basket, and explain this more clearly.

 * For rpart use information as the default split rather than Gini -
makes
   little if any difference.

 * Allow showHelpPlus to have an extra/alternative question that is
   displayed.

 * All random seeds should be 42.

 * Reset kmeans tab on loading a project.

 * Add dozen more weather stations to the weatherAUS dataset.

 * Improve the logic for the display of the Report radio buttons on
the
   Evaluate tab.

 * Spelling correction to a number of tooltips.

Thank you

messages.subject: Re: Prediction for tomorrow?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Rolfe,

On 5 March 2010 23:08, Rolf Edberg <ro...@algonet.se> wrote:
> Hi
>
> I am new to R and Rattle is a great GUI!!

Thanks.

> If I have a time series like the weather data  and want to do a prediction
> about the weather tomorrow and want to use randomForest how do I do that?

There is no native support (yet) for time series in Rattle.

> I import the data and run the Predictive. But where do I put in the data for
> today so I can get a prediction for tomorrow? For example: Rain or Not rain.

Thanks for the question. I've released 2.5.24 - the Evaluate tab now
has a "Enter" data option. Selecting the Score option, and this new
"Enter" option will pop up the R data frame editor to allow you to
enter data yourself, and then have Rattle score it. So you can enter
today's value for the variables and then Rattle will predict rain or
not rain for tomrrow.

Version 2.5.24 is currently propagating through CRAN.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Rattle 2.5.24 released - new score options
messages.body_plain:
Rattle has been updated to CRAN:

  http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rattle/index.html

Changes include:

  * Revamp the help text, and put into the Rtxt translation framework.

  * Fix the height of the data name widget (the library option was growing
    the width for some reason).

  * For Evaluate, add Full and Enter as dataset options. Enter will pop up
    an editor with the final row from the dataset, allowing you to add
    rows or modify the supplied row. We supply the row so that we have an
    example to work from. Full uses the whole original dataset.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Memory problems in R...
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

I am running R 2.10.1 on a Windows XP (with 3+ GB RAM), but with large datasets getting error messages like the following:

Error: cannot allocate vector of size 1.1 Gb

I know there are some workarounds available, but someone told me that R running on a UNIX (or Linux) OS don’t really have this issue given you have large amounts of memory. I would appreciate any comments on this matter.

Cheers,

Ganesh.

messages.subject: Re: Memory problems in R...
messages.body_plain:
On any 32 bit platform you will have limited memory (the address space for memory is 2^32 or something like 4GB). On 64bit you can access a lot more memory. I run GNU/Linux on AMD64 with at least 32GB of memory and plenty of swap space - it would take a bit more to run out of memory in that scenario.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: Memory problems in R...
messages.body_plain:
Your "3+ GB RAM" is not very much. And Linux does not provide memory that is not installed. 3GB in Linux will be the same 3GB that you have with Windows. The R for Windows FAQ has information about how to maximize your memory efficiency. Going to UNIX or Linux will not help and may even hurt since the 64 bit pointers actually consume more memory so if you have less than 4 GB of RAM you may not see much improvement. So unless you are willing to invest in larger amounts of memory at the same time as you switch to an OS with a 64 bit memory manager , you will need to develop some workarounds like sampling.

--
David.
